title: Gauge mean-field theories of the underscreened Kondo lattice
abstract: Various mean-field decoupling schemes have been introduced thus far to study the important and challenging problem of the spin-$1$ underscreened Kondo lattice where magnetic order can coexist with Kondo hybridization. We use a single control parameter $N$ and an unbiased variational ansatz to unify and connect the previously proposed decouplings to standard Read-Newns theory, where fluctuations are small in $1/N$. We compute the corrections around the large-$N$ limit. In particular, we make contact with Nozières strong-coupling theory by finding the residual ferromagnetic Hund interaction that decays logarithmically in the case of a heavy-fermion metal. We map out the ground state phase diagram as a function of $N$ and the Kondo coupling. We find crucial differences between the previously proposed mean-field theories in the strength of the hybridization and total magnetization of the coexistent phase. We show that, within our unifying variational theory, the previously proposed decouplings correspond to either taking $N=2$ from the start, or performing a $1/N$ expansion and then extrapolating to $N=2$. Finally, we summarize the generalization of our theory to $S>1$.
summary: This work develops a unified Gauge Mean-Field Theory to study the spin-1 underscreened Kondo lattice, a model exhibiting competition between magnetic order and Kondo screening. By utilizing a large-$N$ expansion, the authors unify disparate mean-field approaches and map out the ground state phase diagram. The results clarify the nature of the coexisting phases and highlight the role of quantum fluctuations in determining the system's ground state properties.
main_problem: The paper addresses the complex problem of the spin-1 underscreened Kondo lattice (UKL), where magnetic order and Kondo hybridization can coexist.
main_result: The authors develop a unifying variational theory that maps out the ground state phase diagram, revealing crucial differences between previously proposed mean-field treatments.
method: The study employs Gauge Mean-Field Theory (gMFT) using a large-$N$ expansion and an unbiased variational ansatz to calculate fluctuation corrections to the mean-field Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is the spin-1 UKL model, described by a Hamiltonian involving Kondo coupling ($J_K$) and generalized using $N$ replicas of fermionic spin flavors. The theory incorporates local U(1) and SU(2) gauge symmetries.
key_observables: Ground state phase diagram, magnetic moment ($ ar{S}_1$), hybridization ($ ar{V}_1$), and the strength of the residual ferromagnetic Hund interaction.
important_parameters: Control parameter $N$, Kondo coupling $J_K$, and the relative strengths of Kondo energy ($T_K$) versus RKKY energy ($T_{RKKY}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large-$N$ limit for the mean-field theory and uses Gaussian approximations for fluctuation corrections.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate ground state phase diagrams showing three distinct phases (Normal FM, Weak Kondo, Strong Kondo) based on local moment polarization and hybridization, alongside diagrams detailing interaction types (RKKY, Hund's).
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the Hamiltonian and introducing the large-$N$ variational ansatz, proceeds to analyzing gauge field fluctuations and deriving fluctuation corrections ($\Delta H_{fluc}$), and culminates in mapping the full phase diagram and generalizing the theory to $S>1$.
why_interesting: The use of gauge fields and large-$N$ expansions to treat strong correlations and competing orders (magnetic vs. Kondo) is highly relevant to understanding complex quantum materials.
